articles.body: Building a High-Performance E-Commerce Engine for Agricultural Fertilizer Sales: A Developer's Guide E-commerce isn't just about selling dropshipped fast-fashion or subscription SaaS. Some of the most complex, high-transaction-value engineering happens in industries that software developers rarely think about: agriculture. Selling agricultural fertilizers online is a beast of its own. We aren't dealing with fixed-weight 100g packages shipped via standard postal APIs. We are talking about bulk orders, highly volatile seasonal demand, complex hazardous material logistics, strict regional compliance, and tiered B2B pricing structures.

articles.title: A Simple Content Calendar for Freelancers Who Need Consistent Marketing
articles.excerpt: Freelancer marketing often fails for a practical reason: content is treated as a new decision every time. On a busy week, “What should I post today?” competes with client work, admin, and delivery. Th…
articles.body: Freelancer marketing often fails for a practical reason: content is treated as a new decision every time. On a busy week, “What should I post today?” competes with client work, admin, and delivery. The result is either silence or a last-minute post that does not connect to a clear service. A content calendar can help, but it does not need to be a complicated campaign dashboard. A useful version is a small planning system that turns your experience into a few repeatable themes, gives each idea a next step, and leaves room for real client work. This approach is for independent service providers, including virtual assistants, designers, writers, and operations freelancers. It is not a promise of reach, leads, or income.

articles.title: AI Coding Has Made Project-Switching Way Too Easy
articles.excerpt: I have a problem. Actually, I have 84 public GitHub repositories. I checked. Eighty-four. And that's just the public ones. To be fair, they aren't all active projects. Some are old. Some are experimen…
articles.body: I have a problem. Actually, I have 84 public GitHub repositories. I checked. Eighty-four. And that's just the public ones. To be fair, they aren't all active projects. Some are old. Some are experiments. Some are tiny tools. Some have been abandoned, resurrected, renamed, rebuilt, or replaced by another project that I apparently decided absolutely needed to exist. But still. 84. I have always been the kind of person who gets excited about a new idea before I've finished the last one. AI coding tools did not create that problem. They did, however, remove basically every obstacle that used to keep it under control. It used to be harder to start something Not necessarily hard , but there was friction. You'd have an idea. Maybe you'd think about it for a while. Research a library.

articles.title: Track which companies are hiring (and closing roles) with a jobs API
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: I build JOA, the jobs API used below. The code runs on its free plan and I tested it against the live API in early October 2026. Counting live job postings is easy. Knowing which companies…
articles.body: Disclosure: I build JOA, the jobs API used below. The code runs on its free plan and I tested it against the live API in early October 2026. Counting live job postings is easy. Knowing which companies are hiring more and which roles just disappeared is more interesting, and most job feeds can't tell you the second part because a closed role simply vanishes. The Job Opportunities API keeps postings after they leave their source, with a closure date and a reason. This post builds a small hiring tracker on top of that: a daily snapshot of each company's open-role count (so you can see movement over time), the roles posted in the last week, the roles that closed in the last week, with the closure reason, a rough "days listed" figure that is honest about where it came from.

articles.title: Android Auto’s signal bars are finally returning to dashboards
articles.excerpt: Android Auto's signal bars were missing for months, but a fix is finally here.
articles.body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Earlier this year, Android Auto’s cellular signal bars disappeared. Google is now rolling out a fix for the issue. The fix is not yet widely available. If you want to see how strong your cellular signal strength is while you’re driving, you can just look at the signal bar icon on Android Auto. Or, at least, that used to be the case before the icon disappeared earlier this year . While this bug has been a months-long frustration for many Android Auto users, there’s finally some light at the end of the tunnel. It’s hard to believe, but it’s been a little over six months since the initial reports came in. In recent weeks, however, some users said that the signal bars returned after updating to Android Auto v17.8.

articles.title: YouTube is cleaning up one of the worst parts of Shorts
articles.excerpt: Giving low-effort Shorts less room to breathe.
articles.body: TL;DR YouTube is updating Shorts recommendations to prioritize original content and reduce the reach of low-effort reuploads from other creators. Reused clips can still surface if creators add meaningful commentary, editing, storytelling, or another original angle. For viewers, the change should make the Shorts feed feel less repetitive, while creators clipping their own long-form videos likely won’t be affected. YouTube Shorts have never exactly been a fan-favorite feature. From users wanting Shorts to be a standalone app, to YouTube itself letting users set their daily Shorts feed limit to zer o, there’s no shortage of signs pointing to how unhappy many users are with how aggressively short-form video has been pushed across the platform.

articles.body: A critical flaw in GitLab's AI Gateway could let a logged-in user with Duo Agent Platform access run commands on the gateway under certain conditions, GitLab said in an advisory. The gateway is the service that connects a GitLab instance to AI models, and only organizations that host their own gateway need to act. articles.excerpt: Lee esta nota de prensa en inglés aquí. La NASA busca líderes para uno de los puestos más prestigiosos de la Tierra en el ámbito de los vuelos espaciales tripulados: director de vuelo en el control de…
articles.body: El equipo de control de vuelo de Artemis II, en la Sala Blanca de Control de Vuelo del centro de control de misiones del Centro Espacial Johnson de la NASA, en Houston, el 10 de abril de 2026, durante el amerizaje y la recuperación de la misión Artemis II. Crédito: NASA/Robert Markowitz Lee esta nota de prensa en inglés aquí . La NASA busca líderes para uno de los puestos más prestigiosos de la Tierra en el ámbito de los vuelos espaciales tripulados: director de vuelo en el control de misión del Centro Espacial Johnson de la agencia, en Houston. Esta función es fundamental para reforzar el liderazgo estadounidense en la exploración espacial, a medida que la NASA allana el camino hacia una presencia humana sostenida en la Luna.

articles.title: Dots get up in Muse’s business
articles.excerpt: OpenAI's answer to Muse arrived this week, and it looks a whole lot like Muse dressed up in a suit and tie. Dots is a business-first product - for now, at least - costing a minimum of $100 per month.…
articles.body: OpenAI's answer to Muse arrived this week, and it looks a whole lot like Muse dressed up in a suit and tie. Dots is a business-first product - for now, at least - costing a minimum of $100 per month. And sure, you can make a cute little Dot character, just like you can make a cute little Muse character. But OpenAI's early marketing is all about how you can use it to do Business Things: launch websites, reschedule calls, build slide decks for board meetings. Muse, on the other hand, keeps reminding me to buy a jacket I looked at. This week on The Vergecast , we're talking about Dots and the current state of agentic assistants.
